back: A CDN data centre near users where cached content is served from.
Fetches from the origin on the first miss at each PoP, then caches per headers. The default for most content.
You upload content in advance; the CDN never asks an origin. Good for large, stable, bursty files.
A regional cache layer between edge PoPs and the origin, so each object is fetched from the origin about once.
max-age applies to all caches; s-maxage overrides it for shared caches like CDNs.
no-cache: store but revalidate before each use. no-store: never store.
Cache sends If-None-Match with the ETag; unchanged content gets 304 Not Modified with no body.
After expiry, serve the stale copy for up to N seconds while refreshing in the background.
Thousands of distinct values mean thousands of copies per URL, so the hit rate collapses.
What the CDN files a response under: by default host, path and query string plus Vary headers.
Include exactly the inputs that change the response. Too much kills hit rate; too little leaks content between users.
A label on responses so one purge clears every object with that tag (Fastly Surrogate-Key, Cloudflare Cache-Tag).

front: Why prefer versioned URLs to purging?
back: New content gets a new key, so nothing needs purging, caches stay warm, and old pages keep working.
Caching a shared dynamic response for 1–10 seconds to collapse thousands of identical origin requests.
Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, Lambda@Edge, CloudFront Functions: redirects, auth checks, A/B tests, header rewrites.
Hit rate: every miss becomes origin egress, compute and database load.
